text:
tara: Trying to run the quickstart in GitHub Codespaces and getting "Tenant not authorized" on firstcall. Local laptop works. No clear link in the UI to fix billing.

ben: Codespaces doesn't automatically export your local .env. Did you set REDWOOD_ORG or pass X-Redwood-Org header?

tara: I didn't. I assumed the sample would prompt. The response body is:
```json
{"error":"Tenant not authorized","code":"tenant_blocked"}
```

sam: That usually means the request routed to an anonymous tenant that requires billing contact. For cloud quickstarts we should detect missing org info early and surface an actionable hint.

infra-kim: Quick win: change the container entrypoint to emit a clear warning when REDWOOD_ORG is unset and provide a console link. Example echo: "WARNING: REDWOOD_ORG not set. Quickstart will route to an anonymous workspace which may require billing. See https://console.redwood.ai/workspaces"

tara: That would've saved me 20 minutes. Also would be great if the SDK returned a hint in the error when tenant_blocked and no org header present.

ben: Agreed. Proposal for SDK: if code==tenant_blocked && no org header -> append hint: "Set REDWOOD_ORG or X-Redwood-Org, or visit https://console.redwood.ai/workspaces/<id>/billing". Add a unit test covering Codespaces-like envs.

billing-bot: Notice: workspace wz-7b3 requires billing contact. Admins visit https://console.redwood.ai/workspaces/wz-7b3/billing to add payment/contact info.

devex: I'll file two lightweight tasks: quickstart-env-checks and sdk-tenant-block-hint. We'll update the quickstart README to call out Codespaces and CI runners do not copy local env files.

tara: Thanks — after exporting REDWOOD_ORG into Codespaces the sample works. Leaving notes in the onboarding docs. :sparkles:
